need: A flashcard session rail must use the Grammar object that matches each reading job: a state legend must demonstrate the exact treatments used by the question map, while repeated session facts must be rendered as one joined SurfaceListCard.
negativeBoundary: Do not pass plain labels or an independent legend-only color system as proof of question state, do not omit a visually distinct selected-history state, do not substitute a generic SurfaceCard for a repeated label-value list, and do not accept surface count alone as proof of Grammar fidelity.
acceptanceCriteria: Answered, selected-history, current-frontier and future each have an explicit visual treatment when those treatments are distinct in the question map.
Every legend sample uses the same treatment tokens as the corresponding question control; no legend-only semantic color is introduced.
The session-information region renders through SurfaceListCard with separate joined fact rows.
The state legend remains a compact legend rather than being misclassified as a data list.
UAT proves exact Grammar object identity, row anatomy and state-marker mapping in the DOM and rendered viewport.

accepts: A state key whose marks visibly correspond to the question-map treatments.
A joined SurfaceListCard for mode, deck and level facts.
rejects: Three plain labels presented as if they explained three visually different states.
A generic card containing hand-spaced label-value rows.

accepts: Legend samples that visually match answered, selected-history, current-frontier and future controls.
A state model that distinguishes the viewed historical card from the persisted frontier.
rejects: A green answered marker when no answered control uses green.
Three legend states for a question map that visibly renders four states.

review.rationale: Approved after DOM and rendered-viewport proof showed four exact question treatments and a joined SurfaceListCard for session facts on desktop and compact layouts.
